LESSON: WORD CLASS: NOUNS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.1: Word Class: Nouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Word Class: Nouns, part of Strand 3 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: which occur as same in both singular and plural in sentences. 1. Why is it important to use words correctly? 2. Which singular nouns end with letter -s?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify and underline nouns

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify and underline nouns

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Word Class: Nouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration is developed as the learner uses words correctly to construct sentences with peers.

• Digital Literacy is achieved as the learner watches videos on nouns which only occur in singular or plural and

answer questions.

97

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner constructs sentences related to the theme thereby enhancing their awareness

about the need to conserve the environment.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion is promoted as the learner engages in collaborative activities to create and display charts on nouns

occurring as either singular or plural.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link the concept of nouns that exist either as singular or plural to similar concepts in Kiswahili.
